% paragraphs — two paragraph breaks that carry no vertical evidence at all.
%
% One concern: where does one paragraph end and the next begin, when the producer
% sets no extra space between them? This is the case text-styles.pdf was assumed to
% cover and does not. Measured, its four paragraphs are one line each, so every
% consecutive pair is a paragraph boundary and there is no intra-paragraph wrap to
% contrast against — the fixture has no negative case, and a rule that split every
% pair would score full marks on it.
%
% Each paragraph here is deliberately wrapped over three or more lines, which is
% what makes the fixture discriminating: two of the five line pairs are boundaries
% and the other three are ordinary wraps, all at one type size and one leading.
%
% The measurement that motivates the shape. Extracting this document, every
% consecutive line pair steps down 11.955pt against a 9.963pt line height, a ratio
% of 1.200 — identical within a paragraph and between paragraphs, to three decimal
% places. So Tolerance.ParaFrac cannot separate them at any value, and neither can
% Tolerance.SizeFrac, since every line is set at 9.96pt. The only signal left on
% the page is horizontal: a paragraph's first line starts at x=148.712 and its
% continuations at x=133.768, a 14.944pt indent that is exactly three space widths
% of the body font. LaTeX's \parindent is the evidence, and it is the only evidence.
%
% article's default \parskip is 0pt, which is the point rather than an oversight:
% a document that sets space between paragraphs is already handled by the vertical
% step, and would test nothing this fixture is for.
%
% No \noindent anywhere, and the first paragraph is indented like the others.
% \parindent is suppressed on a paragraph immediately after a heading, so a fixture
% that opened with one would hide the signal on the very first boundary.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\pagestyle{empty}

% Hyphenation off, so the fixture tests one thing. Left on, LaTeX broke "contains"
% across a line and the extracted text read "con- tains" — a real defect, and a
% different one: rejoining a hyphenated word is about what a line ending in a hyphen
% means, not about where a paragraph starts. A fixture asserting both would fail for
% either reason and distinguish neither. \sloppy because forbidding hyphenation
% leaves TeX no way to justify some lines and it would otherwise report overfull
% boxes; loose word spacing is invisible to an extractor that measures gaps against
% the font's own space advance.
\hyphenpenalty=10000
\exhyphenpenalty=10000
\sloppy

\begin{document}

The first paragraph runs long enough to wrap across three lines of type, because a
paragraph of one line offers nothing to compare a boundary against. Its second and
third lines begin at the left margin, and that is what makes the indent below
legible as a boundary rather than as ordinary variation.

The second paragraph is indented on its first line and flush on the rest, exactly
as the one above it, and the vertical step between it and the line before is the
same step that separates any two lines here. A reader with only the leading to go
on cannot tell this line from a wrap.

The third paragraph closes the fixture and exists so that the document contains
more paragraph boundaries than it does paragraphs that could be confused for a
heading, since nothing here differs in size or weight from anything else.

\end{document}
